response.sql:
WITH filtered_fees AS (
  SELECT 
    orderslink,
    rebtotal,
    rebrate,
    feerate
  FROM fees
  WHERE rebrate > 0.0005 AND orderslink IS NOT NULL
),
order_stats AS (
  SELECT 
    orderslink,
    AVG(rebtotal) as avg_rebtotal,
    AVG(CASE 
      WHEN rebrate IS NOT NULL AND feerate IS NOT NULL AND feerate != 0
      THEN rebrate / feerate 
    END) as avg_ratio
  FROM filtered_fees
  GROUP BY orderslink
),
global_mean AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) as mean_ratio
  FROM order_stats
  WHERE avg_ratio IS NOT NULL
),
final_calc AS (
  SELECT 
    os.orderslink,
    os.avg_rebtotal,
    os.avg_ratio,
    CASE 
      WHEN os.avg_ratio IS NOT NULL AND gm.mean_ratio IS NOT NULL AND gm.mean_ratio != 0
      THEN os.avg_ratio / gm.mean_ratio
      ELSE NULL 
    END as relative_ratio
  FROM order_stats os
  CROSS JOIN global_mean gm
)
SELECT 
  orderslink,
  avg_rebtotal,
  avg_ratio,
  relative_ratio
FROM final_calc
ORDER BY 
  relative_ratio IS NULL,
  relative_ratio DESC
LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: Fee records with NULL orderslink are excluded from the analysis. Since the request groups by order link, a NULL value does not correspond to a specific order.
Division by zero (feerate = 0) is treated as an invalid calculation, resulting in NULL and excluded from the per-order average (consistent with 'ignoring missing values').
